ratings_why.fun: Astray fights and gap positioning are a good puzzle, but the permanent growth is mostly flat +1/+1 packets, so the board grows slowly and the late game rests on Old Will's one big Start of Combat.
ratings_why.distinct: Making the enemy hit its own side, and treating empty slots as a resource, plays unlike any tribe today and unlike a generic stats tribe.

verdict_why: Two rules contradict or read two ways (Marsh Light and Drowned, Follette's Flit), and the late growth curve could use one more scaling piece.

points.text: Marsh Light goes out before damage, so it can never be Drowned, yet the back-row Johnny line says a self-hit Marsh Light Drowns and pays Hoard-Keeper and Aarnivalkea. Pick one rule and write it on the token.
Mademoiselle Follette's "Your Wisps can Flit twice a fight" reads either as giving every Wisp Flit or as doubling Flit on units that have it. Say which.

Growth is flat: Glim, Foxfire and the Barn Owl give +1/+1 that stops mattering by Tier 5. One mid-tier buffer that scales with your empty slots or with Drownings this game would give the board a curve you watch climb.
Foxfire could give +1/+1 per empty slot next to each Wisp, so the fen build gets a real reason to keep two gaps in the late game.

Early turns pay the gap tax (fewer units, less hero damage) with only Phos and Hobby Lantern at Tier 1. A Tier 1 or 2 unit that rewards an empty slot beside it with stats would make the first turns feel like the tribe.

standouts.why: Fresh-Ink Mapseller turns which slots you leave empty into a targeting choice against the board you can see coming.
Gaffer Turncoat's swap feeding Fingerpost's most-Attack targeting is a real ordering combo, and it answers walls.
Moon in the Mere fills your gaps with copies of your carry: a capstone that pays off the gap plan in one turn.

weakest.why: Lantern Carr Clerk is a plain gold piece whose condition is free early and costly late; it does little for the tribe's idea.
Glowing Barn Owl's once-a-fight +1/+1 is small for Tier 4 and Swoop does not connect to anything else here.
Little Phos does nothing when no enemy is across, and its back-row self-hit is random, so it is a weak seed.

flags.note: Old Will makes a full enemy board spend a whole wave hitting itself; golden Old Will with Jack o' the Turnip likely wipes it. Counterplay is only small boards, Shields and non-attack damage.
Jack o' the Turnip doubles every Astray hit on both sides, stacking with Old Will and Tiddy Mun into one-wave wipes.
Aarnivalkea is uncapped per Drowning, so an Old Will fight against a full board can give five or more +1/+1 to every Wisp each turn.
Can a Marsh Light be Drowned? The token text and the Johnny lines disagree.
Does Follette give Flit to Wisps without it, or only extra uses?
